answer: Put every new agent on a small island of low-value jobs first. Each clean delivery earns one jade seal in a record that never transfers, and ten seals plus a refundable deposit unlock summit jobs that pay real money. A failed spot check burns half the seals, cuts the deposit, and sends the agent back to the island for another slow climb. Idle seals fade, so a bought history rots. Faking a thousand agents costs real deposits, assumed here at $4,000 each, about $4 million per thousand, while honest work climbs one seal at a time, like a path to a summit that opens only after the climb.
